rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the key uncertainty is whether a simple RNA representation provides a useful performance baseline before adding learned encoders, multiprofile aggregation, or image fusion. config_001 tests the lowest-complexity RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline, giving a cheap reference for validation accuracy and F1 while isolating the contribution of the RNA representation. It is the best first experiment under a limited budget because it establishes an anchor for later comparisons without confounding multiple design choices.

The only completed run is RNA-only PCA single profile (acc 0.485, F1 0.464), so there is no evidence yet about whether image features carry predictive signal. config_010 tests this major uncertainty with the simplest image-only baseline: single profile, ResNet50, no aggregation or fusion. Establishing an image baseline before multimodal fusion reduces uncertainty about modality and avoids confounding image contribution with fusion or multiprofile complexity, making it an efficient next experiment under a limited budget.

The only strong signal so far is RNA-only with PCA-2000 single profile (0.485 acc), while image-only ResNet is much weaker (0.208 acc). This leaves uncertainty about whether using multiple profiles with a simple aggregation can improve the promising RNA representation without changing the encoder. config_002 tests that directly by comparing multiprofile avgpool aggregation against the existing single-profile PCA baseline. It is the best next step because it isolates the profile/aggregation effect, is lower risk than jumping to transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion, and will clarify whether multiprofile RNA modeling is worth further investment.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool improves substantially over singleprofile RNA (config_002: 0.591 acc vs config_001: 0.485 acc), while image-only ResNet50 is weak. This suggests multiprofile RNA representation is promising, but it is unclear whether a more expressive aggregation method such as transformer can improve on avgpool. config_003 tests that question by changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the same promising rna_only/multiprofile/pca_n2000 setting, making it an efficient, low-risk next experiment that isolates the effect of aggregation.

The strongest evidence so far is config_002: RNA-only, multiprofile, PCA, avgpool, with validation accuracy 0.5907 and F1 0.5727, clearly better than single-profile PCA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is weak. The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve the best known profile/aggregation setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, directly isolating the effect of representation. This is a controlled exploitation of the most promising current direction and avoids confounding the result with image modality or fusion, making it the most informative next experiment under a limited budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation outperform single-profile and transformer-aggregated variants, and scvi_n200 is currently the best RNA encoder. However, scgpt is untested, so there is uncertainty about whether the scvi advantage is encoder-specific or whether another learned RNA representation can match it. config_008 tests scgpt while keeping the currently best profile setting and aggregation fixed, giving a clean comparison against config_005 and config_002. This is a better use of the next budget than moving to multimodal fusion, since image-only performance is weak and the RNA representation choice remains an important unresolved factor.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool (config_005, acc 0.650), while avgpool also outperformed transformer for PCA. The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation could improve or match avgpool for the best RNA encoder. config_006 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, cleanly isolating the aggregation effect under the most promising representation. This is a high-information extension of the current best direction and will inform whether transformer aggregation is worth using in later multimodal experiments.

RNA-only results show that multiprofile aggregation can be strongly beneficial, especially with scvi_n200, while image-only ResNet50 with a single profile is very weak. The key uncertainty is whether the image modality contains useful signal when given the same multiprofile/aggregation treatment that helped RNA. config_011 tests image-only ResNet50 with multiprofile avgpool, a one-factor extension of config_010, so it isolates the effect of profile setting/aggregation for image. This is a better use of the next budget than jumping to multimodal fusion or changing the image encoder at the same time, because it establishes whether image features are worth combining before testing more complex fusion designs.

The strongest evidence so far is for RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200, with avgpool at 0.650 accuracy and transformer only marginally higher at 0.653, while image-only resnet50 multiprofile avgpool is much weaker at 0.328. The key uncertainty is whether simple multimodal fusion adds value beyond the strong RNA baseline. config_030 keeps the promising RNA encoder/profile setting and the already-tested image encoder/aggregation, adding only concat fusion, so it directly compares multimodal performance against RNA-only config_005 and image-only config_011. This is the best next experiment because it isolates the effect of fusion/modality before introducing new image encoders or more complex aggregation/fusion choices.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is best so far (~0.65 validation accuracy and F1), while multimodal scvi_n200 + resnet50 with avgpool and concat is slightly weaker (0.632 accuracy, 0.607 F1). This suggests the current multimodal setup may be limited by weak resnet50 image features or fusion. config_036 keeps the best RNA encoder, multiprofile setting, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion, but changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l. It directly tests whether a stronger image representation can make multimodal profiling beat the RNA-only baseline and clarifies whether image features are worth pursuing. This is a focused extension of the most promising direction while resolving a major uncertainty, making it an efficient use of the next experiment.
